method: For a real signal confined to fL through fH, bandwidth B=fH-fL and integer zone 1<=n<=floor(fH/B), the non-overlap window is 2fH/n < fs < 2fL/(n-1); zone 1 has no finite upper bound and means fs>2fH. Degenerate zero-width windows and exact boundary rates are excluded so every suggested rate has some ideal margin. The proposed rate is classified directly against all possible integer zones without enumerating a potentially large zone count. Even zones invert the sampled spectrum and odd zones preserve its orientation. Results include 2fH, the theoretical 2B floor (which is not sufficient at every band position), the lowest non-degenerate window and up to twelve lowest-rate windows plus baseband. Frequencies and sample rate use a common Hz/kHz/MHz/GHz unit and are capped at 100 GHz or 100 GS/s. The model assumes no out-of-band energy and does not account for filter transition bands, clock jitter, ADC limitations or other implementation margins.
